characters.summary: Abby Cadabby is a young fairy-in-training on Sesame Street whose magic turns things into pumpkins; she floats when happy and pops in and out of thin air.
weaknesses: Her wand can overload: it once set off too much lightning and broke, and had to be repaired
mobility: Pops in and out of thin air
limitations: Very young (described as 3, later 4) and still a fairy-in-training

sources.supports: Abby Cadabby: fairy-in-training aged 3 then 4; magic includes turning things into pumpkins; pops in and out of thin air and floats when happy; her wand set off too much lightning and broke; casts with 'Zippity-zap!'.

feats.claim: Turns things into pumpkins with her magic.

campaignTags.claim: Fairy who casts spells with a wand ('Zippity-zap!').
Casts spells, e.g. turning things into pumpkins.
Pops in and out of thin air.

unknowns: How high or far she can fly; the source mentions floating, not sustained flight.
Upper limits of her magic as she matures.

characters.summary: Animal is the Electric Mayhem's crazed drummer, kept chained when not performing in his earliest appearance. He is driven by 'sex, sleep, food, drums, and pain' and once grew to ten times his size from Insta-Grow Pills.
weaknesses: Goes wild at the word 'drums', so he can be set off
limitations: Needed restraint: chained in a basement cell when not performing (1975 pilot); later attends anger management

sources.supports: Animal: crazed percussionist; chained in a basement cell in the 1975 pilot; goes wild at the word 'drums'; ate Bunsen's Insta-Grow Pills in The Muppet Movie, grew ten times his size and scared away Doc Hopper; keen sense of smell in Muppets Most Wanted; anger management in The Muppets.

feats.claim: Grew to ten times his size after eating Insta-Grow Pills and scared away Doc Hopper.
Smelled out that Constantine had replaced Kermit.

unknowns: Physical strength outside comedic rage is not documented.
No giant-sized tag: the growth is a one-off pill effect, not his normal size.

notableResults.note: Giant-sized after Insta-Grow Pills; Hopper fled.

characters.summary: Annie Sue is a young female pig singer on The Muppet Show whom Miss Piggy sees as a rival; she is a performer, not a fighter.
weaknesses: No combat training or significant offensive capabilities

sources.supports: Annie Sue: young female pig singer on The Muppet Show; Piggy saw her as a rival and Annie Sue saw Piggy as a role model; helped Fozzie with his memory act in episode 302.

feats.claim: Helped Fozzie Bear with his memory act, easily winning over the crowd.

unknowns: Whether she can defend herself against aggressive opponents

characters.summary: Baby Bear, of 'The Three Bears', is a young Sesame Street bear with a lisp, a fondness for porridge and art, and a perpetual rivalry with Goldilocks.
weaknesses: Not established in the source; no physical feats are documented

sources.supports: Baby Bear: from 'The Three Bears'; lisp; perpetual nemesis Goldilocks; best friend Telly; fond of porridge; interest in art; no physical feats described.

feats.claim: Long-running rivalry with Goldilocks, his perpetual nemesis.

unknowns: Combat capabilities in a serious battle environment

characters.summary: Barkley is a large furry Muppet dog on Sesame Street who behaves like a regular dog and communicates only through barks, yelps and physical contact.
limitations: Communicates only through barks, yelps and physical contact; understands only simple commands such as 'sit' and 'stay'

sources.supports: Barkley: large furry full-bodied Muppet dog, no measurements given; communicates through barks, yelps and physical contact; understands ASL 'sit' and 'stay'; went with Big Bird to China (1982) and Japan (1988).

feats.claim: Accompanied Big Bird on trips to China (1982) and Japan (1988).
feats.citation: Big Bird in China; Big Bird in Japan

unknowns: Exact height and weight are not documented, so no giant-sized tag (owner ruling: about 8 ft or more, documented).

characters.summary: Beaker is Dr. Bunsen Honeydew's long-suffering lab assistant who frequently endures explosions, chemical mishaps, and ray gun blasts. While not a combatant, he possesses high resilience to slapstick destruction.

mechanisms: Extreme cartoon durability against explosions and disintegrators

weaknesses: Constantly subjected to laboratory accidents by Bunsen Honeydew
limitations: Cowardly and lacks offensive combat training

sources.supports: Beaker: victim of Bunsen's experiments, shrunk, cloned, punched, deflated, zapped, turned invisible and blown up, but always comes back for more; electrocuted in The Great Muppet Caper; lives in constant fear.

feats.claim: Has been shrunk, cloned, zapped, turned invisible and blown up in Bunsen's experiments, and always comes back.
feats.citation: The Muppet Show and later productions

unknowns: Whether his resilience extends to sustained magical or cosmic attacks

characters.continuity: Muppets: The Tale of the Bunny Picnic (1986) onward, including The Muppet Christmas Carol (1992)
characters.summary: Bean Bunny is a small, insufferably cute rabbit who starred in The Tale of the Bunny Picnic and later became a routine target of Muppet slapstick violence.

sources.supports: Bean Bunny: debuted in The Tale of the Bunny Picnic (1986), where he helped make peace with the farmer's dog; in The Muppet Christmas Carol he fetched a turkey twice his size for Scrooge; later a routine target of Muppet violence.

feats.claim: Fetched a turkey twice his size for Scrooge on Christmas morning.
Helped make peace with the farmer's dog.
feats.citation: The Tale of the Bunny Picnic (1986)

characters.summary: Beauregard is the dim but lovable janitor of the Muppet Theatre who can effortlessly carry objects far too heavy to carry, though his efforts to help often end in disaster.
weaknesses: Slow-witted: others exploit him for their own purposes
mobility: Drives a taxi (The Great Muppet Caper) and the tour train (Muppets Most Wanted)
limitations: Unfocused and slow to react to threats

sources.supports: Beauregard: dim janitor at the Muppet Theatre; effortlessly lifts objects far too heavy to carry; his efforts often result in disaster; others exploit his slow wit; taxi driver in The Great Muppet Caper; runs the tour train in Muppets Most Wanted.

feats.claim: Effortlessly lifts and carries objects far too heavy to carry.

unknowns: Combat effectiveness if fully motivated to fight

characters.summary: Bernice is Bert's pet pigeon on Sesame Street, played by a real pigeon.

sources.supports: Bernice: Bert's pet pigeon, played by a real pigeon; Bert taught her checkers and she beat him twice in ten games.

feats.claim: Beat Bert at checkers twice in ten games.

campaignTags.claim: A real pigeon (a flying bird) plays her.

unknowns: The source does not describe her flying on screen; the tag rests on her being a real pigeon.

characters.summary: Bert is Ernie's serious, studious roommate who collects paper clips and bottle caps, studies pigeons and loves oatmeal. He avoids physical conflict.
weaknesses: Prone to panic when routines are disrupted
limitations: No combat skills or aggressive tendencies

sources.supports: Bert: serious, studious; collects paper clips and bottle caps (368 bottle caps); eats oatmeal; studies pigeons; pet pigeon Bernice; his nose has come off his face several times.

feats.claim: Collects paper clips and has 368 bottle caps.
